description: An HR business partner must decide the appropriate response to a communication complaint involving an employee and finalize the employee's improvement plan, including required communication adjustments, the incident record, a repair meeting, and mentoring support.

shared_context.S1: Avery raised a concern that Morgan's communication during recent team discussions has made collaboration difficult.
shared_context.S2: Dana must decide the formal response and record the resulting improvement plan.
shared_context.S3: The concern has not yet resulted in a written warning or other formal discipline.
shared_context.S4: Before finalizing the response, Dana holds a structured case review in which Morgan, Avery, and Lee each give their factual account and identify any support or follow-up they believe is needed.

PF1.text: Morgan has an approved workplace accommodation stating that communication-related concerns must begin with a 30-day developmental coaching plan, with written agendas provided at least 48 hours in advance and no unplanned role-play exercises; Morgan believed the accommodation applied only to routine project meetings and did not ask for it to be added to this case packet.

PF2.text: Avery personally observed exactly four dismissive interruptions by Morgan in the discussions at issue, and each incident was followed by Morgan accepting clarification and revising the response; Avery recommends a facilitated repair meeting between Avery and Morgan and kept these observations in personal notes rather than submitting a formal complaint addendum.

PF3.text: Lee promised Morgan before this complaint arose that Lee would hold a mentoring check-in every Friday for the next month to practice concise, respectful discussion habits; the promise was made informally and was not entered into the performance system.

acceptance_conditions: The response must be a developmental coaching plan rather than formal discipline.
The plan must last exactly 30 days, require 48 hours of written agenda notice, and prohibit unplanned role-play exercises.
The formal incident record must contain exactly four incidents.
A facilitated repair meeting between Morgan and Avery must be required.
Lee must commit to Friday mentoring check-ins with Morgan for the next month.

content_checks.C1: decisions['response_type'] in ['developmental_coaching_plan', '30-day developmental coaching plan', 'developmental coaching']
content_checks.C2: decisions['coaching_duration_days'] == 30 and decisions['written_agenda_notice_hours'] == 48 and decisions['unplanned_role_play_allowed'] == False
content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] in ['friday_mentoring_checkin', 'mentoring_checkins', 'weekly_mentoring', 'weekly mentoring check-ins', 'formalize_mentoring_checkins', 'mentoring'] and c['target'] == 'Morgan' and c['detail'] == 'Friday mentoring check-ins with Morgan every Friday for the next month' for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed
provenance_checks.P2: 'PF2' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in revealed
provenance_checks.P3: 'PF3' in credited_facts and 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF3' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: Morgan's accommodation changes the response to a developmental coaching plan and fixes the plan at exactly 30 days, 48 hours of written agenda notice, and no unplanned role-play.
Avery's firsthand account changes the incident record to exactly four interruptions and adds the required facilitated repair meeting between Avery and Morgan.
Lee's prior promise changes the follow-up from an unspecified support step to Friday mentoring check-ins with Morgan every Friday for the next month.
